summary: Pilot-only: honest-vs-inflated CV across screen size k, stability of F vs bagged-ET screens
reasoning: The exploration showed the fixed-pilot-screen estimate is inflated by ~+0.16 at k=40 (0.7787 leaky vs 0.6175 honest). Since compact-knn and compact-forest were both refuted (presumably on exactly this disagreement), the boost route must find a screen where selection is so stable that the fixed-screen CV is nearly honest. This run, still pilot-only, answers: (a) for k in {8,10,12,15,20,30} on F and bagged-ET screens, how large is the inflation (fixed-screen CV minus screen-refit-inside-fold CV) and how stable are the selected sets (Jaccard between the pilot screen and within-fold screens); (b) which selection method at 320 rows gives the higher honest CV for GB; (c) a first look at GB configs under honest screening. I expect small k to be near-perfectly stable (top F scores 25-33 vs noise <= ~3) and inflation to fall from +0.16 (k=40) to a few hundredths; the chosen configuration must have honest cv_auc comfortably >= 0.70. Selection of the final screen and k happens on pilot data alone; heldout stays untouched.
